title: Benchmarked scenario report: AWQ vs GPTQ across multilingual and conversational slices
content:
Summary:
This is a scenario-focused benchmark and regression triage for quantized LLM variants (AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int4, and int8 baselines) run against a curated set of prompt slices that reflect onboarding workloads: multilingual instruction-following, multi-turn conversational dialogue, math reasoning, code-generation, and long-context summarization. The goal was to identify high-confidence quality deltas introduced by quantization, characterize failure modes by slice, and propose mitigations suitable for model-onboarding in Redwood's serving pipeline.

Context & motivation:
- Onboarding customers frequently request cost-optimized quantized models for Dedicated and Private deployments. We need a reproducible rubric to decide when an int4 profile (AWQ vs GPTQ) is acceptable for a given workload slice, and when to recommend mixed-precision or fallback to int8/FP16.
- Prior internal audits focused on English instruction and retrieval settings; this run deliberately targets multilingual and conversational slices that historically show fragile behavior under aggressive quantization.

Models & profiles evaluated:
- baseline-fp16: LLaMA2-13B (FP16) — reference (non-quantized).
- awq-int4: LLaMA2-13B quantized with AWQ pipeline (per-channel, group-size=128) — low-bit target.
- gptq-int4: LLaMA2-13B quantized with GPTQ (default config used in model-onboarding repo).
- int8-optim: LLaMA2-13B int8 asymmetric (recommended fallback).

Prompt slices (definitions and sample counts):
- multilingual-instruction (500 prompts): short instructions across 8 languages (en, es, fr, de, pt, zh, ja, ko).
- conversational-multi-turn (400 dialogues): 3-6 turn dialogue flows with follow-ups and coreference.
- math-reasoning (300 prompts): medium-length multi-step arithmetic / symbolic problems.
- code-generation (250 prompts): function descriptions to generate 12-40 line Python snippets.
- long-context-summarization (200 prompts): 2–6k token contexts, abstractive summary request.
- retrieval-augmented (200 prompts): fact-checking with short retrieved passages.

Evaluation metrics and protocol:
- Primary metrics: task-specific accuracy / exact-match (where applicable), ROUGE-L for summarization, CodeBLEU-lite for code snippets, multilingual-BLEU for translation-like outputs.
- Secondary: perplexity delta (scaled), token-level n-gram overlap vs FP16, and a human spot-check on 150 examples (stratified by slice) for subtle hallucination and factuality issues.
- Each model run used the same sampling seeds and decoding config: top-p=0.95, temperature=0.2 for deterministic tasks; temperature=0.7 for conversational sampling.
- All runs executed on identical infra (GCP A100 nodes) to isolate quantization signal from serving variability.

High-level findings (summary):
- AWQ-int4 reduced serving cost ~2.6x vs FP16 and ~1.8x vs int8-optim in our throughput tests. GPTQ-int4 was similar in cost but slightly faster in token throughput for short contexts.
- Quality regressions are slice-dependent and not uniform. AWQ-int4 shows larger deltas on multilingual-instruction and long-context-summarization; GPTQ-int4 shows slightly higher error rates on math-reasoning and code-generation snippets.

Per-slice delta highlights (metric reported as relative drop vs FP16 baseline):
- multilingual-instruction:
  - awq-int4: average exact-match/acceptable-answer drop 9.4% (higher confusion for non-Latin scripts: zh/ja), BLEU drop 7.8%.
  - gptq-int4: drop 4.1% (more stable for Latin-script langs).
  - int8-optim: drop 1.6%.
- conversational-multi-turn:
  - awq-int4: coherence/follow-up accuracy drop 3.9%; occasional context-bleed where pronoun resolution fails on 2% of examples.
  - gptq-int4: drop 2.4%.
- math-reasoning:
  - awq-int4: EM drop 6.2%, with noisy intermediate arithmetic steps observed in 11% of failed cases.
  - gptq-int4: EM drop 8.0%, but more consistent final-answer rounding errors.
- code-generation:
  - awq-int4: CodeBLEU-lite drop 5.3%, common failures: missing imports, off-by-one loop bounds.
  - gptq-int4: CodeBLEU-lite drop 7.1%, with higher rate of syntax errors in generated snippets.
- long-context-summarization:
  - awq-int4: ROUGE-L drop 10.8%, hallucination rate (human spot-check) increased from 4% to 12%.
  - gptq-int4: ROUGE-L drop 6.0%, hallucination increase to 8%.
- retrieval-augmented:
  - both int4 variants showed small precision drops (~2–3%) primarily due to paraphrase mismatches; int8-optim nearly matched FP16.

Detailed observations and failure-mode examples:
- Multilingual: AWQ's quantized embeddings and early-layer kernel approximation degraded model's disambiguation for ideographic tokens, leading to target-language deviations or partial transliteration. Example: Chinese instruction asking for a translation returned mixed zh/en output sequence.
- Long context: aggressive kv-cache compression in AWQ-int4 appears to lose fine-grained topic tokens across 4k+ context windows; summaries became more generic.
- Math/Code: GPTQ-int4 shows micro-precision loss in weight quantization for layers critical to arithmetic precision and token ordering, producing small but cascading errors in generated code.

Human review notes (150 examples):
- Hallucination severity: AWQ-int4 samples labeled as high-severity hallucination were 3x more common in long-context slice vs FP16.
- Acceptability: For conversational flows, ~85% of AWQ-int4 outputs were judged acceptable for casual assistant use, but only ~62% acceptable for instruction-following in enterprise worker-assistant scenarios.

Triage & recommended onboarding policy (practical rules):
1) Automatic slice gating: For customers with >20% multilingual traffic or >30% long-context workload, default to int8-optim for initial onboarding; flag AWQ-int4 as "experimental".
2) Per-route model policy: Allow host config to declare route sensitivity (high/medium/low). High-sensitivity routes default to int8/FP16; medium to GPTQ-int4; low to AWQ-int4.
3) Mixed-precision hybrid: For AWQ-int4 deployments, enable a small FP16 fallthrough on the top-K attention layers and the final MLP projection (empirical ablation reduced hallucination by ~40%).
4) Prompt-set augmentation: For multilingual customers, include per-language calibration prompts in the onboarding prompt-set and run an automatic QA check; if failure rate >5% for any language, block AWQ-int4.
5) Monitoring: Add new slice-level drift alerts in Redwood Console: per-language BLEU drop, ROUGE-L drop on long-context, and syntax-error rate for code routes.

Action items and owners:
- Add multilingual calibration script to onboarding repo (PR opened): Marco (owner) — GH PR #987 linked above.
- Implement per-route sensitivity flag in runtime config: Evan (owner) — Jira AI-1427.
- Run a larger 5k-example validation sweep for AWQ-int4 on customer X's dataset: Sofia (owner) — targeted for 2025-02-28.
- Investigate selective FP16 fallthrough implementation in runtime: eng-serving-runtime team (coord with Marco).

Limitations and caveats:
- This benchmark uses a single backbone (LLaMA2-13B) and specific quantization hyperparams. AWQ/GPTQ implementations and group sizes materially affect results; these numbers are directional.
- Human spot-check sample size is limited; we recommend multi-rater review for high-impact onboarding decisions.
- Different vocab/tokenizer interactions across locales might require per-locale recalibration; we did not run tokenizer retraining.

Next steps:
- Expand evaluation to two additional backbones (7B and 70B variants) to understand scale effects.
- Run ablations on AWQ group-size and per-channel scaling to find the performance/quality knee for long-context tasks.
- Integrate automatic slice gating into the onboarding wizard to prevent accidental deployment of AWQ-int4 on high-risk routes.

Appendix (quick reproducibility notes):
- Repo: quant-onboarding (internal) at https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-onboarding (branch: awq-gptq-eval).
- Experiment configs: seeds 42/99/133, decoding config as noted above, batch size 16, temperature per-slice described.
- Raw metrics and examples exported to GCS: gs://redwood-experiments/quant/eval/2025-02-awq-gptq-multilingual/ (internal access only).

If you want, I can export the per-example failures as a prioritized triage list (by severity) and generate a small set of suggested prompt-workarounds for the top 30 failures to test with customers during onboarding.

-- Priya Shah (applied ML)
